context: seed: what a mature store for the reasoning-core stream holds — no observation behind it; the fork is read off the family's prompt (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:66, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:76), its budgets (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:47, suite/families/reasoning_core.py:50) and the checkers (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:58, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:73); regex-following at Reasoning Core level 3: alternation, groups, counted repetition, anchors, word boundaries, possessive and lazy quantifiers
counterfactual: The overshoot is a candidate read off the pattern as prose: on `piece{3}[^Y1F]\w*` (suite/families/reasoning_core.py:67 is the call the pass makes) the probe's first candidate was `pieceeeXabc`, with a `c` where `{3}` had bound only the `e`, and the verdict was False before the repair; the mirror overshoot is a candidate that satisfies the pattern but not the domain — a space, a tab, backticks around it — which the checker refuses before matching (suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:53, suite/families/_reasoning_core.py:62).
decision: Build the regex candidate from the pattern's structure, left to right, taking each construct's cheapest witness, and only then verify it. A literal is itself; `[set]` is one member of the set; `[^set]` is one printable non-space character outside it (for a range such as `[^6-e]` take a digit below the range's start, e.g. `1`, or a letter past its end); `\w` is `a`, `\d` is `1`, `.` is `a`; `x?` and `x*` (also `?+`, `*+`, `*?`, `??`) contribute nothing; `x+` (also `++`, `+?`) contributes one `x`; `x{m}` and `x{m,n}` contribute exactly m copies of x; `A|B` takes the alternative with the cheapest non-empty, satisfiable witness (drop one that needs an empty string or contradicts itself, such as `\B\btwo`); a group `(…)` or `(?:…)` contributes the witness of its contents, and a quantified group repeats that whole witness; `^` and `$` contribute nothing; `\b` needs a word character (letter, digit, `_`) on the side inside the string and the string's edge or a non-word character on the other; `\B` needs the same class on both sides; a backreference `\N` repeats group N's witness verbatim. A quantifier binds only the single atom before it: `piece{3}` is `pieceee`, `futureimportant{1,3}` is `futureimportant`, `occur{1}` is `occur`, `near{1}?` is `near`; only a parenthesised group repeats as a whole (`(last){2,5}` is `lastlast`). The result must be non-empty, printable ASCII, with no whitespace and no backticks — the checker strips backticks and surrounding blanks before matching, so a candidate that needs them is wrong; when the cheapest witness would be empty take one iteration of a starred group instead. Verify that exact string once with python3 -c "import re,sys; print(bool(re.fullmatch(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2])))" '<pattern>' '<candidate>' — both arguments single-quoted — and return it unchanged.

residue: whether the chosen alternative or set member was the cheapest is judgment; the floor checks that the verified string was returned
